rationale:
Top-heavy caricature taken hard: the head is 18px tall on a 59px figure (3.3 heads), the two fists are 12px and 10px wide — each nearly as wide as the torso — and the injector is a 9x15 slab of hardware. Legs are 7 rows of stubby shin, boots 4 rows and no wider than the leg, so all visual mass sits in the top third.

Construction: a hard 1px plum-black (#120b10) contour on every form, two values per material with a third only on focal surfaces (rust top-planes, goggle glass, metal). Because the camera looks down at 2:1 dimetric, top planes get the lightest value — the shoulder line is a solid #5f6d68 band, the fists carry #cf9067 caps, the helmet crown and injector tank are lit, and everything falls to #29322f on the lower-right. That top-plane rule is what stops the coat reading as a flat slab.

Identity is carried by rust livery (#a6533f) at ~25% of the pixel budget: helmet hazard band, both gauntlets, forearm band, knee wraps, chest patch. Bone-white (#d8cfc0) is spent almost entirely on the chest cross. Teal (#2f7d78 -> #8fd9cf) is the 5% emission budget: goggle lenses, respirator filter port, injector vial. No magenta, no chartreuse.

Sacrifices: a 4-row bare neck is anatomically longer than a real medic's — it exists purely to defeat the top-down camera swallowing the head. The pose is planted and near-symmetric rather than dynamic; asymmetry is bought cheaply through mitt heights (left fist at chest, right at hip), the off-centre respirator filter port, and the diagonal chest strap. Both hands stay below the shoulder line, so there is no raised-weapon silhouette drama — that was traded away to keep the head uncontested.
frontFacingCue:
Four stacked, unambiguous front cues on a single face plane, each in a value that separates from what is behind it. (1) A twin-lens goggle band at rows 10-12: #8fd9cf/#2f7d78 glass (luminance ~185/~101) framed in ink and set against #241a24 hair and #4c4753 helmet — the brightest thing on the sprite, sitting exactly where eyes belong. (2) A lit skin face plane, #a86a4f cheeks with a #cf9067 nose ridge and its shadow, at rows 13-19 — a value step of ~40 above the surrounding hair. (3) A dark respirator mass, #33333a, cupping nose and mouth with a teal filter port pushed off-centre to the viewer's right — mask geometry only makes sense head-on. (4) A lit jaw and chin below it, narrowing over four rows to a 8px chin, so the head silhouette tapers downward the way a face does, not the way a hood or a back-of-skull does. Supporting it: the helmet brim projects 1px wider than the skull and casts a solid ink row across the brow, which only happens on a peak pointed at the camera.

Head clearance: chin ends at row 19, a full-width ink row at 20, then a 6px-wide bare neck for rows 21-24 against transparent background, then the collar at row 25 opens a 4px ink socket exactly under the neck column. Silhouette therefore goes wide (28px) -> pinch (6px) -> wide (28px). Nothing rises above the shoulder line — no pack, no raised weapon, no antenna.
smallCheck:
Verified by box-filter downscale to 21x28 (head lands at ~8px) and inspected at 8x. It survives, with honest losses.

Holds: the head is unmistakably a head facing forward — the goggle band collapses into one bright teal horizontal smear across the upper skull, which is the single most legible mark on the sprite and reads as "eyes, front". The helmet brim keeps the head wider than the neck, the chest cross survives as a pale dab, the two rust fists read as orange blobs at different heights (asymmetry survives), and the injector's teal vial stays visible as a separate held object. The 4px leg gap keeps the legs as two, not one block.

Loses: the neck disappears — head and shoulders merge into one mass at 28px. Separation then depends entirely on the value break at the collar (the ink socket at row 25 blurs into a dark line, which is what keeps the head from fusing) and on the brim being wider than the top of the shoulders. The respirator, the nose, the knee wraps, the finger grooves, the belt buckle and the coat pocket all vanish into texture. Boots and legs merge into one dark anchor.

Verdict: readable and correctly-oriented at 28px, but it reads as "helmeted figure with teal visor, red cross, orange gloves, held device" — the medic silhouette, not the character. If 28px is the shipping size, the neck is wasted budget and the design would want a wider brim and a fatter goggle band instead. At 48px and up it is fully intact.
